paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul says there are two ways to belong to God's family, and only one of them works. One way is through the flesh, bound up with the covenant from Mount Sinai, and Paul says it bears children into slavery (Galatians 4:23-24). The other is through the promise, and Paul says the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother (Galatians 4:26).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Paul tells the believers, "Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise" (Galatians 4:28). You don't earn your place at the table by checking boxes, because it was given to you through the promise. And when he ends, he says, "Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman" (Galatians 4:31).

Now, Paul also says the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit, and "It is the same now" (Galatians 4:29). I think that means the Galatians shouldn't be shocked when things get hard. But hard doesn't change who you are, and the free woman's children share in the inheritance (Galatians 4:30). That's the kind of news that makes me want to dive face-first into the chocolate chips, so go on and stand in your freedom, friend!
